messages.author: ea4e687a14dc225c
messages.subject: Need more control over legends
parts:
Hi falks, I was playing with following lines of codes :

library(ggplot2)
dat1 <- matrix(rnorm(60), nrow=20); dat1
dat2 <- data.frame(value=as.vector(dat1), variable=rep(c(paste("var",
1:3, sep="")), 20))
dat4 <- data.frame(value1=apply(dat1, 2, "mean"), variable=paste
("var", 1:3, sep=""))
ggplot(dat2) + geom_point(aes(y=value, x=1:20, colour=factor
(variable)), size=3.5, alpha=0.6) +
geom_hline(aes(yintercept=value1, colour=variable), data=dat4)


If I look into legend then I would see in color description that, it
mirrors both straight line and point, to explain color asif points are
overlapped on straight line. Is it possible to have any one of them
i.e. either point or straight line there? Because in my present case,
it is sufficient to have any one to explain color.

Thanks,

messages.author: 373beb702917b8b5
messages.subject: Re: Need more control over legends
parts:
Hi Megh,
I don't see that any good will come from removing either the line of
point indicator in the legend. Both lines and points are colored, and
the color has the same meaning, so the legend combines the two in
order to save space. What do you hope to gain by removing one of the
geom indicators?

-Ish

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Need more control over legends
parts:
You want to turn off the legend for a scale, not for a layer, so try this code:

library(ggplot2)
library(maps)
states <- map_data("state")

ggplot(data=states, mapping=aes(x=long, y=lat)) + theme_bw() +
geom_polygon(aes(group=group, fill=region), alpha=0.4) +

borders("state", size=0.5, colour="white") +
scale_fill_discrete(legend = F)
